title: Moral Realism Stance Analysis Schema
description: Structured analysis of a philosopher's stance on moral realism. Classifies the metaethical position, maps key commitments across core dimensions, and evaluates supporting arguments, vulnerabilities, and dialectical status.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this moral realism analysis run

position_classification.description: Classification of the metaethical position regarding moral realism

key_commitments.description: Core metaethical commitments mapped across five key dimensions

cognitivism.description: Whether moral judgments express beliefs (cognitivist), non-cognitive attitudes (non_cognitivist), or a mix

truth_aptness.description: Whether moral claims are capable of being true or false

mind_independence.description: Degree of mind-independence attributed to moral facts or properties

moral_facts_exist.description: Whether moral facts exist in any sense

naturalism.description: Whether moral properties are natural, non-natural, or supernatural

supporting_arguments.description: Arguments offered in support of this metaethical position

argument_name.description: Name or brief label for the supporting argument

vulnerabilities.description: Known vulnerabilities or objections to this position

objection.description: Name or label of the objection

standard_response.description: Standard reply or defense available to the position

dialectical_status.description: Current dialectical standing of the position in the literature

dominance.description: Prevalence of this position in the contemporary literature

trend.description: Direction of change in popularity or support

key_proponents.description: Key philosophers associated with this position

key_opponents.description: Key philosophers arguing against this position
